standard.title: Australia's representation: states, territories and Countries/Places
standard.description: the representation of contemporary Australia as states and territories, and as the Countries/Places of First Nations Australians prior to colonisation, and the locations of Australia's neighbouring regions and countries
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y2 (AC9HS2K03): Students located their home within geographical divisions from local to state/territory and explored interconnections across scales.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify how Australia can be represented as states/territories and as Countries/Places of First Nations Australians, and locate Australia's neighbouring regions and countries.

nodes.label: States, territories and capitals
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can name and locate Australian states and territories and their capital cities on a map.
nodes.minimum_width: Name at least four states or territories and locate them on a map.
nodes.typical_width: Use geographical tools (globe, wall map, digital source) to locate and name all states and territories and their capital cities; label them on a map.
wider: Research differences between states and territories in terms of population, size and climate
Locate Australian states and territories on a globe and discuss Australia's position relative to the equator and hemispheres
nodes.hinge_reason: Locating states and territories is prerequisite to comparing them with Countries/Places of First Nations Australians — you cannot compare boundaries you cannot locate.

response_modes.reason: Accurate map knowledge requires repeated practice — use map quizzes, labelling and digital tools to build locational fluency.

success_criteria: Names at least four states or territories correctly
Locates at least four on a map

nodes.label: Countries/Places of First Nations Australians
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use the AIATSIS Map of Indigenous Australia to compare Aboriginal Countries and Torres Strait Islander Places with surveyed state/territory boundaries.
nodes.minimum_width: Use the AIATSIS map to identify at least two Aboriginal Countries or Torres Strait Islander Places and compare their boundaries with state/territory lines.
nodes.typical_width: Compare the AIATSIS map of Indigenous Australia with a states and territories map; identify how boundaries differ; gain an appreciation of the different ways Australia can be represented; discuss what the two maps reveal about different understandings of land.
wider: Investigate why Aboriginal Country boundaries differ from state/territory lines and what determined each type of boundary
Explore how the existence of two different maps of Australia reflects two different ways of belonging to and organising land

response_modes.reason: The comparison of two fundamentally different map representations requires scaffolded reasoning — what does each map show, why do they differ, what does each represent?

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Comparing the AIATSIS map with the states/territories map creates a genuinely provocative geographic inquiry that challenges students to think about what maps represent and whose knowledge they encode.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two Aboriginal Countries or Torres Strait Islander Places on the AIATSIS map
Describes at least one difference between the AIATSIS map and the states/territories map

nodes.label: Neighbouring regions and countries
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can locate Australia's neighbouring regions and countries and identify the direction of each from Australia.
nodes.minimum_width: Locate at least three neighbouring countries (e.g. Papua New Guinea, New Zealand, Indonesia) on a globe or digital source and identify their direction from Australia.
nodes.typical_width: Use a globe or digital source to locate Pacific Island nations, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste, Indonesia and other relevant countries; label them on a map; identify direction from Australia.
wider: Investigate one neighbouring country in depth and describe its relationship with Australia
Compare Australia's location relative to its neighbours with the location of another country relative to its neighbours

response_modes.reason: Locating neighbouring countries requires map practice — use interactive digital tools and repeated labelling exercises.

success_criteria: Locates at least three neighbouring countries on a map or globe
Identifies the direction of at least two neighbouring countries from Australia
